title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: From fictitious professors to midnight organ recitals, Brown University's traditions reflect its unique blend of intellectual rigor and creative spirit.

cards.title: The Van Wickle Gates Procession
cards.subtitle: Opening Convocation and Commencement
cards.notes: Walk through the center gates only twice: once inward as a freshman and once outward as a graduate. Passing through more often is said to curse your graduation or marriage prospects.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial passage through the university's main gates marking the beginning and end of a student's journey.
cards.evidence_claim: The center gates remain closed except for Opening Convocation (opened inward) and Commencement (opened outward).
cards.access_notes: The center gates are physically locked except during specific university ceremonies.

cards.title: Carberry Day
cards.subtitle: Every Friday the 13th
cards.notes: Donate loose change to 'cracked pots' for the Carberry Fund on Friday the 13th. It honors Brown's fictional Professor of Psychoceramics, legendary for his 'future late wife' Laura.
cards.short_summary: A recurring celebration of Brown's most famous fictitious professor, occurring every Friday the 13th.
cards.evidence_claim: Every Friday the 13th is Carberry Day, where funds are collected in cracked pots for the Josiah S. Carberry Fund.
cards.source_title: Brown Traditions: Josiah S. Carberry | Alumni & Friends
cards.access_notes: Donation pots are typically placed in university libraries and dining halls on the designated day.

cards.title: Midnight Halloween Organ Recital
cards.subtitle: October 31st at 11:59 PM
cards.notes: Bring a blanket and pillow to Sayles Hall to hear spooky classics on the 1903 Hutchings-Votey pipe organ. Costumes are encouraged for this atmospheric midnight performance.
cards.short_summary: An annual midnight concert featuring haunting music on one of the world's largest remaining pipe organs.
cards.evidence_claim: The annual Halloween Midnight Organ Recital takes place October 31st at 11:59 pm in Sayles Hall.
cards.source_title: 2025 Halloween Midnight Organ Recital | Events | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Entry is limited to the first 450 students with ID; others can watch a livestream on the Main Green.

cards.title: Campus Dance
cards.subtitle: Commencement Weekend
cards.notes: Dance under thousands of paper lanterns on the College Green. This multi-generational ball brings together alumni and graduating seniors to kick off Commencement weekend.
cards.short_summary: A massive outdoor dance party under paper lanterns that serves as the official start of Reunion and Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Dance transforms the heart of College Hill into an open-air ballroom with glowing paper lanterns.
cards.source_title: Campus Dance | Alumni & Friends | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Tickets are required for entry; the event is held on the Friday evening of Reunion Weekend.

cards.title: The Pembroke Seal Curse
cards.subtitle: Alumnae Hall Steps
cards.notes: Avoid stepping on the bronze seal on the steps of Alumnae Hall. Legend says women who step on it will get pregnant, and men will never graduate.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition regarding a bronze seal that students carefully avoid to protect their academic and personal futures.
cards.evidence_claim: A decades-old myth warns that stepping on the Pembroke Seal leads to pregnancy for women or failure to graduate for men.
cards.source_title: Walking through the Van Wickle Gates: Commencement and campus curses
cards.access_notes: The seal is located on the steps leading to Alumnae Hall on the Pembroke Campus.

cards.title: The Ratty Sit
cards.subtitle: Sharpe Refectory
cards.notes: Spend an entire day—from opening at 7:30 AM to closing at 7:30 PM—inside the 'Ratty' dining hall. It is a rite of passage for students testing their endurance and appetite.
cards.short_summary: A student-led endurance challenge involving staying in the main dining hall for its entire operating duration.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'Ratty Challenge' involves students spending the entire day at the Sharpe Refectory.
cards.source_title: Which activities top Brown students' bucket lists?
cards.access_notes: Requires a meal swipe or payment for entry; students must remain inside the facility to complete the challenge.

cards.title: Spring Weekend
cards.subtitle: Annual Music Festival
cards.notes: Enjoy a weekend of live music on the Green. Organized by the Brown Concert Agency since 1950, it has hosted legends from Bob Dylan to Kendrick Lamar.
cards.short_summary: Brown's signature annual music festival featuring major national acts and student performers.
cards.evidence_claim: Spring Weekend is a student-organized music festival hosted annually in April at Brown University.
cards.access_notes: The event is typically free for Brown students but requires a wristband for entry to the fenced concert area.

cards.title: Senior Sing
cards.subtitle: Commencement Finale
cards.notes: Join the graduating class on the steps of Sayles Hall for a final musical tribute. This tradition dates back to the mid-19th century as part of Class Day celebrations.
cards.short_summary: A sentimental musical tradition where graduating seniors gather to sing together one last time.
cards.evidence_claim: Graduating seniors take to the steps of Sayles Hall for the time-honored Brown tradition: Senior Sing.
cards.source_title: Campus Dance | Alumni & Friends | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Occurs late Friday night during Commencement weekend following Campus Dance.

cards.title: The Baccalaureate Procession
cards.subtitle: Multi-faith Service
cards.notes: Follow the Chinese lions and drumming groups to the First Baptist Church. This service blends diverse spiritual traditions with the medieval custom of 'sermonic oration.'
cards.short_summary: A colorful, multi-faith procession and service for graduating seniors held in the historic First Baptist Church.
cards.evidence_claim: The Baccalaureate ceremony includes a procession led by Chinese lions and Japanese drumming groups.
cards.source_title: A distinctly Brown take on an age-old tradition — Class of 2016 celebrates Baccalaureate
cards.access_notes: Seating inside the church is reserved for seniors; guests can watch via livestream from other locations.

cards.title: Gigs on the Grass
cards.subtitle: Fall Student Music Showcase
cards.notes: Catch local student bands and solo acts performing all day on the Main Green. It is a relaxed fall tradition that showcases the diverse musical talent within the student body.
cards.short_summary: A day-long outdoor concert series featuring student performers on the university's central lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Gigs on the Grass presents student acts throughout the day on the Main Green.
cards.source_title: Gigs on the Grass to take on Main Green Saturday
cards.access_notes: Open to the public and held outdoors on the university's main lawn.
